__ Hon'ble Shri Justice Narendra Kumar Vyas Order on Board 19.10.2023 1.

This is the second bail application filed by the applicant under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, for grant of anticipatory bail, who has apprehension of being arrested in connection with Crime No. 136/2023, registered at Police Station- Pulgaon, District- Durg (C.G.) for the offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 34 of IPC.
2. Earlier first bail application filed by the applicant bearing MCRCA No. 579 of 2023 was rejected by this Court vide order dated 13.07.2023.
3. Case of the prosecution, in brief, is that the present applicant along with his father Mahaveer Agrawal are engaged in the business of sale and marketing of petrol.

It is alleged that the present applicants induced the complainant Deepak Sahu to pay the amount of money on multiple occasion under a false promise to secure the license and other NOC for the establishment of BPCL Gas Agency.
It is further alleged that the applicant prepared a fake LOI and cheated the complainant.
It is alleged that neither the amount was returned to the complainant nor the Gas agency of BPCL gas was provided to the complainant, there by the offence has been committed.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant would submit that the applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in the case.
He would further submit that the applicant runs the petrol pump and the complainant is not an ordinary layman but belongs to the privileged section of the society.

He would further submit that complainant Deepak Sahu is the husband of Nayab Tahsildar who was posted as Tahsildar at the relevant point of time and has jurisdiction over the petrol pump run by the applicant.

The complainant in the month of October- November 2021 approached the present applicants with an LOI for establishment of the Gas Agency and sought assistance from the applicant for the reason that he was engaged in similar business.
The applicant advised the complainant to apply for approval/NOC from the local administrative offices.
The complainant himself applied in various offices including the office of the Collector and the office of the Food Department who have granted LOI, thus, it cannot be said the LOI is forged.
He would further submit that the complainant along with his wife who was posted as Tahsildar exercised superior dominating position over the businesses run by the applicant.

The complainant acting in connivance with his wife demanded illegal gratification from the applicant on various occasions and threatened him with dire consequences, therefore, the applicants may be granted benefit of anticipatory bail.
5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State as well as counsel for the objector oppose the anticipatory bail application.

Counsel for the objector has filed reply to the application contending that the applicantshave produced the forged medical certificate from Medanta Hospital,therefore,
action was taken against them.
Complainant has filed the complaint wherein he has stated that he has paid Rs. 5 lakhs to the applicant against which the applicant submitted forged LOI to him.

He would submit that on 25.03.2023 the complainant told him that he will arrange a meeting at Durg,
therefore, he along with his father had gone to Durg and contacted him on his Mobile No.
9630007568 in the office of Bharat Petroleum Office where he has stated that he came to the Bharat Petroleum Office Raipur but he did not turn up when they contacted to mobile no. 9425272888, the applicant No.1 told that his son Sahil Agrawal is admitted in the hospital and the complainant demanded his money then the applicants threatened him with dire consequences, therefore, the applicant is not entitled to get benefit of anticipatory bail.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
7.

The subsequent development has taken place that the applicant has paid Rs. 6 lacs through Demand Draft No. 227695 dated 30.08.2023 drawn by State Bank of India, Branch- Industrial Estate, Bhilai in favour of the complainant- Deepak Kumar Sahu, which has been forwarded to him by his counsel and the complainant has accepted the same.
A copy of the demand draft is taken on record.

8. Considering this aspect of the matter and the fact that the applicant has already made good the default by paying Rs. 6 lacs to the complainant through the demand draft, I am inclined to extend the benefit of Section 438 of the Cr.P.C. to the applicant.
9.

Accordingly, the instant anticipatory bail application is allowed and It is directed that in the event of arrest of the applicant in connection with the aforesaid offence, he shall be released on anticipatory bail by the officer arresting him on executing a personal bond in sum of Rs. 25,000/-

(ii) That the applicant shall not, directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat undue influence to the prosecution witnesses;
(iii) That the applicant shall appear before the trial Court on each and every date given to them by the said Court till disposal of the trial.
